jointly $C^1$ of [[def-em-fields]], the source fields $\rho,J$ are continuous
of [[def-em-sources]], the constants are those of [[def-em-si-conventions]],
the force density is
$f:=\rho E+J\times B$ of that clause (ii), in
$\mathrm N\,\mathrm m^{-3}$, and $g,\sigma,\Pi=-\sigma$ are the momentum
density, Maxwell stress and momentum flux of
[[def-em-vacuum-stress-momentum]]. Then:

(a) [Local identity] On $\Omega\times I$, componentwise,

$$\partial_tg-\operatorname{div}\sigma=-f,\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad\partial_tg+\operatorname{div}\Pi=-f,$$

that is, $\partial_tg_i-\sum_{j=1}^{3}\partial_j\sigma_{ij}=-(\rho E_i+(J\times B)_i)$ for every $i$, with $\partial_t$ the partial derivative at fixed position and $\operatorname{div}$ taken at fixed time.

(b) [Fixed-volume identity] Let $\Omega'\subseteq\Omega$ be open with
$\overline{\Omega'}\subseteq\Omega$ carrying the finite piecewise $C^1$
presentation of
[[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-piecewise-c-one-domains]], let
$t_0<t_1$ with $(t_0,t_1)\subseteq I$, assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]), and let $n$ be the outward unit normal. Then for
every $t\in(t_0,t_1)$ and every $i$,

$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\Omega'}g_i\,dx=\oint_{\partial\Omega'}\Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^{3}\sigma_{ij}n_j\Bigr)dS-\int_{\Omega'}f_i\,dx=-\oint_{\partial\Omega'}\Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^{3}\Pi_{ij}n_j\Bigr)dS-\int_{\Omega'}f_i\,dx,$$

theorem.

force density $f$ is defined only for the matter model of clause (ii), so no
claim is made about a prescribed current without such a matter model. No
conservation of field-plus-matter momentum follows without explicit matter
balances and their boundary fluxes. The field-momentum rate in (b) is the
boundary traction minus the integrated matter force; these terms can cancel,
and neither may be discarded without justification. The weak branch, singular sources and
non-integrable products are excluded as in
[[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]]; no self-force, radiation reaction or
magnetic-monopole coupling is included, in accordance with the exclusions of
[[post-em-lorentz-coupling]]. This is not an empirical claim.

Retain the fields $E,B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ of [[def-em-fields]], the
energy density $u$ and Poynting vector $S$ of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]],

[[def-em-si-conventions]], and the partial derivatives $\partial_j$ of

$g:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ defined by

$$g:=\frac{S}{c^2}=\varepsilon_0\,E\times B,$$

in $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-2}\mathrm s^{-1}$; the second equality uses

$$\sigma_{ij}:=\varepsilon_0\Bigl(E_iE_j-\tfrac12\delta_{ij}\lvert E\rvert^2\Bigr)+\frac{1}{\mu_0}\Bigl(B_iB_j-\tfrac12\delta_{ij}\lvert B\rvert^2\Bigr),$$

$\epsilon_{ijk}=+1$ if $(i,j,k)$ is an even permutation of $(1,2,3)$,
$\epsilon_{ijk}=-1$ if it is an odd permutation, and $\epsilon_{ijk}=0$ if two
indices coincide, in the positively oriented basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$. The object
$\ell$ carries $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-1}\mathrm s^{-1}$ and the components
of $x\times\Pi$ carry $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm s^{-2}=\mathrm N\,\mathrm m^{-1}$.

chart: under a shift $x\mapsto x+a$ of the origin by a constant $a\in\mathbb R^3$
their values become $\ell+a\times g$ and $x\times\Pi+a\times\Pi$ respectively,
so the definition fixes one origin in the laboratory frame and every statement
about $\ell$ or $x\times\Pi$ is relative to that fixed origin.

identity and no interpretation of $\sigma$ or $\Pi$ as force or momentum flux
is asserted here; every balance identity involving these objects is the content
of the separate theorem items of this page.

(g) [Quadratic character and singular support] All five objects are quadratic
in the fields $E,B$. For a locally integrable branch of
[[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] the exclusions recorded in
[[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]] apply to each of them: the products
$E_iE_j$, $B_iB_j$ and the components of $E\times B$ need not be locally
integrable, no product of distributions is defined, and the displayed formulas
then define the objects pointwise almost everywhere, the framework using them
only where the local integrability of the products is separately established.
No value is assigned at a point of singular source support.

(h) [No covariant object] No four-dimensional or covariant interpretation of
$(u,S,g,\sigma)$ is defined here; in particular $g$ is not identified with the
spatial components of a covariant momentum density.

Assume the hypotheses of [[pthm-em-momentum-balance]]: the smooth branch of
[[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]], clause (ii) of [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]], the
jointly $C^1$ fields of [[def-em-fields]], continuous sources, and the force
density $f=\rho E+J\times B$. Let $g$, $\sigma$, $\Pi=-\sigma$, the orbital
angular momentum density $\ell=x\times g$ and its flux $x\times\Pi$ be those
of [[def-em-vacuum-stress-momentum]] relative to the origin fixed there. Then:

(a) [Local identity] On $\Omega\times I$,

$$\partial_t\ell+\operatorname{div}(x\times\Pi)=-x\times f,$$

componentwise
$\partial_t\ell_i+\sum_{j=1}^{3}\partial_j(x\times\Pi)_{ij}=-(x\times f)_i$,
where $(\operatorname{div}(x\times\Pi))_i:=\sum_{j=1}^{3}\partial_j(x\times\Pi)_{ij}$
and $(x\times f)_i=\sum_{j,k=1}^{3}\epsilon_{ijk}x_jf_k$ with the Levi-Civita
symbol of [[def-em-vacuum-stress-momentum]], and $\partial_t$ is the partial
time derivative at fixed position
([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]).

(b) [Fixed-volume identity] Under the domain, time-interval and
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ hypotheses of [[pthm-em-momentum-balance]](b), and with
$n$ the outward unit normal, for every $t\in(t_0,t_1)$ and each $i$,

$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\Omega'}\ell_i\,dx=-\oint_{\partial\Omega'}\Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^{3}(x\times\Pi)_{ij}n_j\Bigr)dS-\int_{\Omega'}(x\times f)_i\,dx,$$

the closed-surface integral being the finite face sum of the divergence
theorem used in that clause.

(c) [Scope] The identities depend on the origin fixed in
[[def-em-vacuum-stress-momentum]](e) through the explicit factor $x$; no
field-only conservation follows by dropping the boundary flux: (b) retains
both that flux and the integrated torque, which can cancel to give a zero
field-angular-momentum rate. Conservation of field-plus-matter angular
momentum requires explicit matter balances and their boundary fluxes. The hypotheses and exclusions of
[[pthm-em-momentum-balance]](c) are inherited. The density $\ell$ is orbital,
$\ell=x\times g$; no spin or intrinsic angular momentum of matter is defined
or claimed by this item. This is not an empirical claim.

Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, let $c \in A$ be a limit point of $A$
([[def-limit-point-r]]), let $f, g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ be differentiable at $c$
([[def-derivative]]) and let $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$. Then:

1. $f + g$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(f+g)'(c) = f'(c) + g'(c)$;
2. $\alpha f$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(\alpha f)'(c) = \alpha f'(c)$;
3. $fg$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(fg)'(c) = f'(c)g(c) + f(c)g'(c)$;
4. if $g(c) \ne 0$ then, writing $A_0 := \{\, x \in A : g(x) \ne 0 \,\}$, the
   point $c$ lies in $A_0$ and is a limit point of $A_0$, the quotient
   $(f/g)|_{A_0} : A_0 \to \mathbb{R}$, $x \mapsto f(x)/g(x)$, is differentiable
   at $c$ as a function on $A_0$, and
   $$\bigl((f/g)|_{A_0}\bigr)'(c) \;=\; \frac{f'(c)\,g(c) - f(c)\,g'(c)}{g(c)^{2}} .$$

Each claim asserts two things: that the derivative on the left exists, and that
it has the stated value. Both are proved.

vanishes, and $g$ may vanish at points of $A$ far from $c$; restricting to $A_0$
is forced. That the restriction still has $c$ as a limit point, so that a
derivative there means anything at all, is not free either, and it is the last

[[thm-caratheodory-characterisation]].** No difference quotient is estimated and

$$D_vf(a):=\lim_{t\to0}\frac{f(a+tv)-f(a)}{t}.$$

For a standard basis vector $e_j$ ([[lem-standard-basis-of-f-n]]), $D_{e_j}f(a)$ is the **$j$th partial derivative**, written $\partial_jf(a)$. These are ordinary vector-valued one-variable derivatives in the sense of [[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]].

**Set form.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, [[def-countable-choice]]), used to establish the Lebesgue measure space of [[thm-lebesgue-measure-is-a-complete-measure]]. Let $K\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be compact, Lebesgue measurable and of finite Lebesgue measure $\lambda_n(K)<\infty$, let $a<b$, and let $f$ be a real-valued function, defined and continuous together with its partial derivative $\partial_tf$ on an open neighbourhood of $K\times[a,b]$ in $\mathbb R^{n+1}$. Then $t\mapsto\int_Kf(x,t)\,d\lambda_n(x)$ is differentiable at every $t\in(a,b)$ with

$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_Kf(x,t)\,d\lambda_n(x)=\int_K\partial_tf(x,t)\,d\lambda_n(x),$$

and at $t=a$ and $t=b$ it has relative (one-sided) derivatives, taken within $[a,b]$, both equal to the same displayed integral. Equivalently, for every $t\in[a,b]$ and every sequence $h_k\to0$ with $h_k\ne0$ and $t+h_k\in[a,b]$,

$$\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{1}{h_k}\Bigl(\int_Kf(x,t+h_k)\,d\lambda_n(x)-\int_Kf(x,t)\,d\lambda_n(x)\Bigr)=\int_K\partial_tf(x,t)\,d\lambda_n(x).$$

**Surface form.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, [[def-countable-choice]]) for the surface measure of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]. Let $S$ be a fixed compact embedded $C^1$ hypersurface in $\mathbb R^m$, $m\ge2$, and let $f$ be real-valued, defined and continuous together with $\partial_tf$ on an open neighbourhood of $S\times[a,b]$. Then $t\mapsto\int_Sf(\sigma,t)\,dS(\sigma)$ is differentiable in the same relative sense with

$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_Sf(\sigma,t)\,dS(\sigma)=\int_S\partial_tf(\sigma,t)\,dS(\sigma).$$

The statements are pointwise in $t$ and make no claim about moving parameter sets $K(t)$ or $S(t)$, about singularities crossing $K$ or $S$, about differentiability of $\partial_tf$, or about differentiation in the spatial variables; only the one-dimensional parameter $t$ is differentiated. Integrals are Lebesgue integrals, and the surface integrals are those of the cited surface measure; the case $K=\varnothing$ or $\lambda_n(K)=0$ is included and the two sides vanish.

All integrals are finite. In a specified finite gluing, the two fluxes on every shared face cancel.

Let $f:X\to[0,+\infty]$ be measurable and let $E$ be measurable with $\mu(E)=0$.
Then
$$\int_E f\,d\mu=0.$$

Let $I \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be order-convex ([[def-interval]]) and let
$f : I \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $I$ ([[def-continuity-real]]) and
differentiable at every point of $I$ that is interior to $I$
([[def-interior-closure-boundary-r]], [[def-derivative]]), with

$$f'(x) = 0 \qquad \text{at every interior point } x \text{ of } I .$$

Then $f$ is constant on $I$: there is a real $k$ with $f(x) = k$ for every
$x \in I$.

Consequently, if $f, g : I \to \mathbb{R}$ are both continuous on $I$ and both
differentiable at every interior point of $I$, with $f'(x) = g'(x)$ at every
interior point $x$, then there is a real $k$ with

$$f(x) \;=\; g(x) + k \qquad \text{for every } x \in I .$$

**Order-convexity of $I$ is essential and is not a convenience.** The
conclusion is false on a domain that falls into separate pieces, since a
function may be constant on each piece with different constants; nothing in the
proof would survive, because the mean value theorem is applied to the segment
joining two points of the domain and that segment must lie in the domain.

**The hypothesis is imposed only at interior points.** At an endpoint of $I$
nothing is asked at all: $f$ need not be differentiable there, and the proof
never evaluates a difference quotient at an endpoint, since it applies the mean
value theorem on a segment $[u,v] \subseteq I$ and uses the derivative only at
points of $(u,v)$, all of which are interior to $I$. What is *not* meant is that
the derivative at an endpoint is free to be nonzero: once $f$ is known to be
constant its difference quotient at an endpoint is constantly $0$, so wherever
$f'$ exists at an endpoint it is $0$ too. That is a consequence of the theorem,
not a hypothesis of it.

Finally, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be open. A tensor field here is a matrix-valued map $\Pi:U\times I\to\mathbb R^{3\times3}$; assume its entries and all spatial first partial derivatives are continuous and $\Pi_{kj}=\Pi_{jk}$. Let $g,f:U\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous, assume the componentwise time derivative $\partial_tg$ exists, and suppose $\partial_tg+\operatorname{div}\Pi=-f$ on $U\times I$, where $(\operatorname{div}\Pi)_i=\sum_{\ell=1}^{3}\partial_\ell\Pi_{i\ell}$ and $(x\times\Pi)_{i\ell}:=\epsilon_{ijk}x_j\Pi_{k\ell}$ with the sum over $j,k$. Then the vector field $x\times g$ and the tensor field $x\times\Pi$ satisfy

$$\partial_t(x\times g)+\operatorname{div}(x\times\Pi)=-x\times f .$$

energy density $u$ and Poynting vector $S$ of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]],

position in the spatial chart, $\delta_{ij}$ for the Kronecker symbol

basis. Let $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and $\mu_0>0$ be the constants of
[[def-em-si-conventions]].

$\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$.

(b) [Maxwell stress tensor] The **Maxwell stress tensor** is the spatial
tensor field $\sigma$ on $\Omega\times I$ with components

$$\sigma_{ij}:=\varepsilon_0\Bigl(E_iE_j-\tfrac12\delta_{ij}\lvert E\rvert^2\Bigr)+\frac{1}{\mu_0}\Bigl(B_iB_j-\tfrac12\delta_{ij}\lvert B\rvert^2\Bigr),$$

and its **flux tensor** is the spatial tensor field $x\times\Pi$ with
components

$$(x\times\Pi)_{i\ell}=\sum_{j,k=1}^{3}\epsilon_{ijk}\,x_j\,\Pi_{k\ell}.$$

Here $\epsilon_{ijk}$ is the Levi-Civita symbol, defined by
$\epsilon_{ijk}=+1$ if $(i,j,k)$ is an even permutation of $(1,2,3)$,
